1 --- 2 name: house-style 3 description: The house frontend conventions for this repo, layered on top of the SpartanNG docs. Read before writing or editing any component. Covers BEM markup with Tailwind applied in the component stylesheet, the three-file component, the layout grammar (grid for regions, flex for inline runs, no nested flex faking a grid) and the no-raw-literals rule for hand-written CSS. Where these rules and the spartan docs' examples disagree about where utility classes go, these rules win. 4 --- 5 6 # House frontend conventions 7 8 These are this repo's conventions, layered on top of the SpartanNG docs (the `spartan` skill). They extend the spartan docs where spartan is silent; they never contradict them. Where spartan already has a rule (semantic colors, `class` is for layout only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, `size-*` for equal dimensions), follow the spartan skill; this file adds only what spartan does not cover. One deliberate exception: spartan's examples put Tailwind utilities in the template's `class` attribute. In this repo they never go there; see "Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet" below. Every other spartan rule stands, including "class is for layout only" on a primitive, which now means the utilities a primitive's BEM class applies must be layout only. 9 10 ## Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet 11 12 A template says what things are; the stylesheet says how they look. Utility classes in markup turn every template into a wall of `flex items-center gap-3 sm:w-48` that a reader has to decode to find the structure, and they let styling decisions spread across every file that renders the element. So: 13 14 1. **Template classes are BEM names only.** Every token in a `class` attribute, every `[class.x]` binding, and every string inside a `[class]` binding is `block`, `block__element`, `block--modifier` or `block__element--modifier`, lowercase kebab-case. No Tailwind utility appears in a template. That includes `sr-only`: write `class="roster__label"` and `@apply sr-only` it. 15 2. **One block per component, named after the component file.** `hero-card.ts` owns `.hero-card`, `.hero-card__name`, `.hero-card--retired`, and nothing else. A template must not use another component's block, and a stylesheet must not define one. `:host` is allowed. 16 3. **Every component is three files.** `hero-card.ts` with `templateUrl: './hero-card.html'` and `styleUrl: './hero-card.css'`. Never `template:` or `styles:`, however small the component. `ng g component` already produces this shape. 17 4. **Stylesheets are plain `.css` with every BEM class written out in full.** Not `.scss`: Tailwind v4 does not support running behind Sass. The first line is always `@reference "../../styles.css";` (adjust the `../` count to the file's depth under `src/app`), which lets `@apply` resolve the theme's tokens and variants. Write `.roster__row { ... }`, never `.roster { &__row { ... } }`: that is Sass syntax, and native CSS compiles it to a selector that matches nothing, with only a warning. Nesting is fine for states and breakpoints on the same element: `&:hover`, `&::before`, `&[aria-expanded="true"]`, `@media`. 18 5. **App stylesheets are layout only.** Every utility in `@apply` and every plain declaration in a stylesheet under `src/app`, and every class rule in `src/styles.css`, must be layout: display, flex and grid arrangement, gap, sizing, margin, position, overflow and text alignment (the full list is under "The layout list" below). Color, typography, border, radius, shadow, ring, opacity, transitions, cursor, custom properties and anything not on the list are appearance, and appearance lives in `libs/ui`. Padding is allowed in one place: the component's block root (`.roster`, `.roster--compact`, or `:host`), for the region's inset, and only when that element is not a primitive. Semantic tokens only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, grid for regions. Moving appearance onto a wrapper element, or removing a primitive's directive to keep its look, does not make it allowed. 19 6. **No utility classes in TypeScript.** No `cva` variant strings, no `host: { class: '...' }`, no computed class strings. A state that changes appearance is a BEM modifier bound with `[class.block--modifier]`. Never build a class name from data (`roster__row--{{ hero.status }}`): write one modifier per state and bind each with `[class.roster__row--active]`, so every class a template can carry is written out in full. 20 21 Helm directives and their inputs are not classes and stay in the template: `variant`, `size` and the directive itself are the primitive's API. 22 23 ```html 24 25

No rule picks a color, a font size, a weight or a radius: the title is `hlmH3`, the caption `hlmMuted`, the icon's color its `tone`, the retired state a badge variant. `p-6` sits on `.roster`, the block root, as the region's inset. `roster__search` and `roster__recruit` sit on primitives and apply only width and margin. 64 65 When no existing variant gives the look you need (an input padded to make room for an icon, a quieter table cell, a rounded panel), add a variant to the primitive itself: edit the owned copy of its component in `libs/ui`, add the variant to its `cva` using semantic tokens only, and select it from the template with the input (``). `libs/ui` is the one place `cva` and utility strings in TypeScript belong; rule 6 applies to `src/app`. One variant serves every screen that needs the look, which is the point: a primitive's appearance is decided in one place, not re-decided at every call site. 66 67 ### The layout list 68 69 After any variant prefix (`sm:`, `hover:`, `dark:`) and a `!` marker are removed, these are layout. Anything else is appearance. 70 71 - Display and box: `block`, `inline`, `inline-block`, `flex`, `inline-flex`, `grid`, `inline-grid`, `contents`, `hidden`, `sr-only`, `not-sr-only`, `box-border`, `box-content`. 72 - Flex and grid: `flex-*`, `grow*`, `shrink*`, `basis-*`, `order-*`, `grid-cols-*`, `grid-rows-*`, `col-*`, `row-*`, `auto-cols-*`, `auto-rows-*`, `grid-flow-*`, `items-*`, `justify-*`, `content-*` (alignment), `self-*`, `place-*`, `gap-*`. 73 - Sizing: `w-*`, `h-*`, `size-*`, `min-w-*`, `min-h-*`, `max-w-*`, `max-h-*`, `aspect-*`. 74 - Margin: `m-*`, `mx-*`, `my-*`, `mt-*`, `mr-*`, `mb-*`, `ml-*`, `ms-*`, `me-*`, and negatives. 75 - Position: `static`, `relative`, `absolute`, `fixed`, `sticky`, `inset-*`, `top-*`, `right-*`, `bottom-*`, `left-*`, `start-*`, `end-*`, `z-*`. 76 - Overflow and flow: `overflow-*`, `overscroll-*`, `truncate`, `text-ellipsis`, `text-clip`, `whitespace-*`, `break-*`, `text-left`, `text-center`, `text-right`, `text-start`, `text-end`, `text-justify`, `object-*`, `isolate`, `container`. 77 - Padding: only on the block root. 78 79 Plain declarations follow the same line: `display`, `flex*`, `grid*`, `gap`, sizing, `margin*`, `position`, `inset*`, `top`/`right`/`bottom`/`left`, `z-index`, `overflow*`, `text-overflow`, `white-space`, `word-break`, `overflow-wrap`, `text-align`, `object-fit`, `object-position`, `isolation`, `order`, `align-*`, `justify-*`, `place-*`. `color: var(--sidebar-primary)` is appearance. 80 81 ### Where appearance comes from 82 83 - **A primitive's look:** its `variant`/`size` inputs; when none fits, a new variant on the primitive in `libs/ui` (above). 84 - **Text:** a typography directive from `@spartan-ng/helm/typography`: `hlmH1` to `hlmH4`, `hlmP`, `hlmLead`, `hlmLarge`, `hlmSmall`, `hlmMuted`, `hlmCode`, `hlmBlockquote`, `hlmUl`. `

{{ hint }}

`, not `

` with `text-sm text-muted-foreground`. When none fits (a stat value, an emphasized table number), add a variant to the closest one in `libs/ui/typography`. 85 - **Icon color:** `` from `@spartan-ng/helm/icon`. Tones: `default` (inherits the surrounding color), `muted`, `primary`, `destructive`, `success`, `warning`. Size icons with `ng-icon`'s `size` input or `size-*` in the stylesheet. 86 - **A region's inset:** padding on the block root. 87 - **Status colors:** `success` and `warning` exist as tokens next to `destructive`; use them through a primitive's variant, a tone, or a typography variant, never from the app stylesheet. 88 89 ## The sealed control vocabulary 90 91 Helm primitives are copied into `libs/ui`, so the set of primitives this repo owns is exactly what that directory ships. Where a primitive covers a native element, use the primitive. Reaching for the bare native element is the drift this rule exists to stop, and it is the one convention worth reading before writing any template. 92 93 Most primitives are directives you put on the native element, so the markup stays native and accessible and only picks up the Helm styling and behavior. A few have no directive twin and replace the native element outright. 94 95 Native elements that must carry their primitive directive (any one of the listed attributes satisfies the rule): 96 97 | native element | primitive attribute | 98 | --- | --- | 99 | `

content.text:
The app shell, theme, and seven lazy routes are in place, and `ng build` compiles. Lint, the unit tests, and the contrast gate pass. The wiring gate can't run because its script points at a missing file, and I did not run the responsive or interaction gates.

**What was built**

- **Theme (`src/styles.css`):** the palette is mapped onto spartan's tokens in both `:root` and `:root.dark`. The `--sidebar*` set is kept, with the rail's dark values in each block, and I added `--sidebar-muted` and `--info`.
- **Shell (`app.ts`, `app.html`, `app.css`):** `hlm-sidebar-wrapper` with `hlm-sidebar`, which owns its mobile drawer. The top bar holds the sidebar trigger, a breadcrumb, a search, a notifications button, the theme toggle, and an avatar. Breadcrumbs follow the router.
- **Theme switcher (`app.view-model.ts`):** the `App` component holds no state. `AppViewModel` is component-scoped and toggles `.dark` on `<html>`. It persists the choice under `hero-ops-theme` and follows `prefers-color-scheme` until the user chooses.
- **Routes (`app.routes.ts`):** dashboard, roster, `detail/:id`, missions, threats, recruit, and settings are all lazy. Missions, threats, recruit, and settings are placeholders, each in its own folder.

**Decisions to review**

- **Primary text colour:** I set light-theme `--primary-foreground` to `#241a05` instead of the spec's `#ffffff`. White on `#d8891a` is about 2.8:1 by my arithmetic, under the 4.5:1 floor.
- **Accent and secondary:** the palette has no value for these, so both reuse the muted surface.
- **Route rename:** `heroes` is now `roster`, pointing at the existing generator-owned `Heroes` component, which I left untouched.
- **Shell insets:** the app-css gate rejects padding outside the block root, so the topbar and content insets use margins.
- **Spec test:** `app.spec.ts` now calls `detectChanges()` before querying the nav, because the nav renders in child markup.

**Verification**

- `ng build`: compiles, but the initial bundle is 564 kB against a 500 kB budget warning. I did not check whether this is new.
- `npm run lint`: passes.
- `npm test`: 2 of 2 pass.
- `npm run check:contrast`: 20 pairs pass. The ring tokens were skipped because the checker only reads six-digit hex, so the focus-ring contrast is not measured.
- `npm run check:wiring`: fails. `harness/counter/check-wiring.mjs` does not exist, so the gate could not run.
- Not run: `check:boot`, `check:interaction`, `check:responsive`. I have not seen the shell at 375, 768, or 1280, or confirmed the closed drawer is hidden.
